question.text: Let ABC be a triangle. Consider four points $\mathrm{p}_{1}, \mathrm{p}_{2}, \mathrm{p}_{3}, \mathrm{p}_{4}$ on the side AB, five points $p_{5}, p_{6}, p_{7}, p_{8}, p_{9}$ on the side $B C$, and four points $p_{10}, p_{11}, p_{12}, p_{13}$ on the side AC. None of these points is a vertex of the triangle ABC. Then the total number of pentagons, that can be formed by taking all the vertices from the points $\mathrm{p}_{1}, \mathrm{p}_{2}, \ldots, \mathrm{p}_{13}$, is $\_\_\_\_$
